How far apart two meters read

Source: R/agreement.R
power_agreement.Rd

Reports the Bland-Altman summary for every pair of sources in every run: the mean difference, the spread of that difference, and the limits of agreement within which most seconds fall. The gain is the same thing on a multiplicative scale, which is usually the more natural way to read a power meter's error, since meters tend to be a few per cent out rather than a fixed number of watts out.

Usage

power_agreement(aligned, min_power = 0, block = 60, replicates = 1000)

Arguments

aligned

Result of align_rides().

min_power

Both sources must exceed this to count, in watts.

block

Bootstrap block length in seconds.

replicates

Number of bootstrap replicates.

Value

A tibble with one row per source pair per run:

run, source_a, source_b

The pair and the session it came from. source_a sorts before source_b alphabetically, and every difference is source_a minus source_b.

seconds

Paired seconds behind the row, after coasting and anything below min_power is dropped.

bias_w, bias_lo, bias_hi

Mean difference in watts, with its 95% bootstrap interval.

sd_difference

Standard deviation of the per-second difference.

loa_lo, loa_hi

Limits of agreement, bias_w +/- 1.96 SD: the range most individual seconds fall within. Not an interval on the mean, and much wider than one.

gain_pc, gain_lo, gain_hi

The same difference multiplicatively, as a percentage, with its 95% bootstrap interval. Usually the more natural reading.

Details

Intervals come from a moving-block bootstrap, not from treating each second as independent.

See also

Other agreement: agreement_by_level(), level_dependence()

Examples

aligned <- read_rides(demo_rides()) |> align_rides()
power_agreement(aligned)
#> run1: assioma reads 2.6% higher than kickr (95% CI 2.4 to 2.7, from 1,800 seconds)
#> run2: assioma reads 0.6% lower than quarq (95% CI -0.5 to 1.7, from 1,800 seconds)
#> 
#> # A tibble: 2 × 13
#>   run   source_a source_b seconds bias_w bias_lo bias_hi sd_difference loa_lo
#>   <chr> <chr>    <chr>      <int>  <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>         <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 run1  assioma  kickr       1800   4.74    4.23    5.18          5.86  -6.74
#> 2 run2  assioma  quarq       1800  -4.19   -6.96   -1.67         11.0  -25.7 
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: loa_hi <dbl>, gain_pc <dbl>, gain_lo <dbl>, gain_hi <dbl>
